newsitem.title: RUSSIA: EBRD extends 127 mln mark loan to St Petersburg.
newsitem.headline: EBRD extends 127 mln mark loan to St Petersburg.

text.p: The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development said on Friday it would extend a 127 million mark loan to St Petersburg for its 300 million mark programme to improve sewage and water supply services.
The loan to St Petersburg's water and sewage company Vodokanal will be divided into two tranches of 55 million marks and 72 million marks, EBRD said in a statement.
The loan will be paid back over 10 years and will be guaranteed by St Petersburg and backed by a separate project support undertaking from the Russian government, it said.

"It is the first time that a multilateral financial institution has provided a loan to a municipal utility on a non-sovereign basis, without any state or commercial bank guarantee," said Johan Bastin, Director of the EBRD's Municipal and Environmental Infrastructure Team.
Last month St Petersburg placed its debut Eurobond on international markets. Standard & Poor's assigned the city a credit rating of BB- and IBCA a BB+.
The Nordic Investment Bank and governments of Denmark, Finland, Germany and Sweden will also contribute to the project, which will reduce pollution in the Baltic Sea.
